title: Esther Chapter 3 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Esther chapter 3 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Esther Chapter 3 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Esther Chapter 3.

questions.question: In Esther 3, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Mordecai did not bow to Haman
The king's servants bowed to Haman
questions.explanation: This is the first event mentioned in the chapter. (Esther 3:1)

questions.question: Who did King Ahasuerus promote?
questions.explanation: King Ahasuerus promoted Haman the son of Hammedatha. (Esther 3:1)

questions.question: What was Haman's lineage?
questions.explanation: Haman is described as the son of Hammedatha the Agagite. (Esther 3:1)

questions.question: What command did the king give concerning Haman?
questions.explanation: The king commanded that all the king's servants should bow and reverence Haman. (Esther 3:2)

questions.question: Who did not bow or show reverence to Haman?
questions.explanation: Mordecai bowed not, nor did him reverence. (Esther 3:2)

questions.question: What did the king's servants ask Mordecai?
options: Why he transgressed the king's commandment
questions.correctAnswer: Why he transgressed the king's commandment
questions.explanation: The king's servants asked Mordecai why he transgressed the king's commandment. (Esther 3:3)

questions.question: What did Mordecai tell the king's servants?
questions.explanation: Mordecai told them that he was a Jew. (Esther 3:4)

questions.question: How did Haman feel when he saw that Mordecai did not bow?
questions.explanation: Haman was full of wrath when he saw that Mordecai bowed not. (Esther 3:5)

questions.question: What did the king's servants do daily regarding Mordecai?
questions.explanation: They spake daily unto him. (Esther 3:4)

questions.question: What did Haman see regarding Mordecai's behavior?
questions.explanation: Haman saw that Mordecai bowed not, nor did him reverence. (Esther 3:5)

questions.question: Haman was promoted above whom?
questions.explanation: Haman was set above all the princes that were with him. (Esther 3:1)

questions.question: True or False: Mordecai is a Jew.
questions.explanation: Mordecai told the king's servants that he was a Jew. (Esther 3:4)

questions.question: True or False: All the king's servants bowed to Haman.
questions.explanation: All the king's servants bowed and reverenced Haman as commanded by the king. (Esther 3:2)

questions.question: True or False: Haman was a servant of Mordecai.
questions.explanation: Haman was promoted by the king and was above all the princes, not a servant of Mordecai. (Esther 3:1)

questions.question: True or False: Mordecai showed great reverence to Haman.
questions.explanation: Mordecai did not show reverence to Haman as he bowed not. (Esther 3:2)

medium.title: Esther Chapter 3 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Esther Chapter 3 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What did Haman seek to destroy in Esther 3:6?
questions.explanation: Haman sought to destroy all the Jews that were throughout the whole kingdom of Ahasuerus, as stated in Esther 3:6.

questions.question: What does Esther 3:8 promise will happen if someone does what Esther 3:2 commands?
questions.explanation: Esther 3:2 emphasizes the king's command to bow to Haman, and disobeying this command, as Mordecai did, led to severe consequences.

questions.question: How many talents of silver did Haman offer to pay for the destruction of the Jews?
questions.explanation: In Esther 3:9, Haman offered ten thousand talents of silver to those who would carry out the destruction of the Jews.

questions.question: What consequence does Esther 3:7 suggest about the casting of Pur?
options: It was done to decide the fate of the Jews
questions.correctAnswer: It was done to decide the fate of the Jews
questions.explanation: Esther 3:7 indicates that the casting of Pur was used to determine the timing for Haman's plans against the Jews.

questions.question: What did Mordecai refuse to do according to Esther 3:2?
questions.explanation: Mordecai refused to bow or show reverence to Haman, as stated in Esther 3:2.

questions.question: What was the nature of the people Haman spoke about to the king in Esther 3:8?
options: They were loyal to the king
questions.explanation: Haman described the Jews as a certain people scattered abroad and having diverse laws, as mentioned in Esther 3:8.

questions.question: What did the king give to Haman in Esther 3:10?
questions.explanation: The king took his ring from his hand and gave it to Haman, as stated in Esther 3:10.

questions.question: How did Mordecai's actions affect Haman according to Esther 3:5?
questions.explanation: Mordecai's refusal to bow to Haman filled Haman with wrath, as stated in Esther 3:5.

questions.question: What does Esther 3:9 imply about Haman's intentions?
options: He wanted to enrich the king
He wanted to destroy the Jews
He was seeking revenge on Mordecai
He was acting out of jealousy
questions.correctAnswer: He wanted to destroy the Jews
questions.explanation: Haman explicitly requested the king to write a decree for the Jews' destruction, indicating his malicious intentions as per Esther 3:9.

questions.question: What did Haman think of Mordecai according to Esther 3:6?
questions.explanation: Haman thought scorn to lay hands on Mordecai alone, indicating his contempt for Mordecai, as stated in Esther 3:6.

questions.question: What does Esther 3:4 reveal about Mordecai's identity?
options: He was an enemy of Haman
He was a servant of the king
questions.explanation: Mordecai identified himself as a Jew when he was questioned about his refusal to bow, as stated in Esther 3:4.

questions.question: Did the king know of Haman's plot against the Jews at the time of Esther 3:8?
questions.explanation: At the time of Esther 3:8, the king was unaware of Haman's plot against the Jews, as Haman was presenting it for the first time.

questions.question: Is it true that Haman acted out of personal grievance against Mordecai according to Esther 3:6?
questions.explanation: Haman's scorn for Mordecai led him to seek the destruction of all the Jews, revealing that personal grievance was a key motivator, as stated in Esther 3:6.

questions.question: Is it false that Esther was unaware of Haman's plans until later in the story?
questions.explanation: Esther was not part of the conversation between Haman and the king in Esther 3:8, indicating she was unaware at this point.

questions.question: Is it false that Mordecai showed reverence to Haman according to Esther 3:2?
questions.explanation: Mordecai did not bow or show reverence to Haman, which is a key point in Esther 3:2.

hard.title: Esther Chapter 3 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Esther Chapter 3.

questions.question: What authority did King Ahasuerus give to Haman in Esther 3:11?
options: The silver is given to thee, the people also, to do with them as it seemeth good to thee.
Only the silver is given to thee.
The people are given to thee, but not the silver.
Haman must seek the king's permission before acting.
questions.correctAnswer: The silver is given to thee, the people also, to do with them as it seemeth good to thee.
questions.explanation: Esther 3:11 states explicitly that the king gave Haman both silver and people to act upon as he saw fit.

questions.question: On what day were the king's scribes called to write the decree according to Esther 3:12?
options: The thirteenth day of the first month
The first day of the first month
The thirteenth day of the twelfth month
The first day of the twelfth month
questions.correctAnswer: The thirteenth day of the first month
questions.explanation: Esther 3:12 specifies that the scribes were called on the thirteenth day of the first month to write the decree.

questions.question: What was the scope of the letters sent out as described in Esther 3:13?
options: To destroy, kill, and cause to perish all Jews, young and old, children and women, in one day
To summon all Jews to the palace
To exile the Jews to a distant land
To collect taxes from the Jews
questions.correctAnswer: To destroy, kill, and cause to perish all Jews, young and old, children and women, in one day
questions.explanation: Esther 3:13 clearly states the letters commanded destruction of all Jews regardless of age or gender on one day.

questions.question: Which month is identified as the time for the destruction of the Jews in Esther 3:13?
questions.explanation: Esther 3:13 names the twelfth month, Adar, as the day when the destruction will occur.

questions.question: How was the decree communicated to the diverse peoples of the kingdom according to Esther 3:12?
options: According to the writing thereof, and to every people after their language
Only in the king's native tongue
questions.correctAnswer: According to the writing thereof, and to every people after their language
questions.explanation: Esther 3:12 specifies the decree was written according to the writing and in every people's language to ensure comprehension.

questions.question: What was the reaction of the city Shushan after the decree was given according to Esther 3:15?
questions.explanation: Esther 3:15 states that after the decree, the city Shushan was perplexed, showing confusion and distress.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'Pur' (פּוּר) in Esther 3:7 mean?
questions.explanation: In Esther 3:7, the Hebrew word 'Pur' refers to a 'lot' drawn to determine the date, indicating a method of casting lots.

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently used in Esther 3:13 describing the decree to destroy the Jews?
questions.explanation: Esther 3:13 foreshadows the upcoming conflict and deliverance by detailing a decree for destruction, setting the stage for later reversal.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of the enemies' plans being overturned as seen in Esther 3:6?
questions.explanation: Acts 4:27-28 reflects the theme of hostile plans against God's people, similar to Haman's plot in Esther 3:6, showing divine sovereignty over enemies.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage provides historical context to Haman's Agagite origin mentioned in Esther 3:1?
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 15:8 records King Saul's attack on Agag, king of the Amalekites, providing historical context for Haman's Agagite lineage in Esther 3:1.

questions.question: What event immediately precedes the king giving Haman his ring in Esther 3:10?
options: Haman offers to pay ten thousand talents of silver
Mordecai refuses to bow to Haman
The king's servants report Mordecai's disobedience
questions.correctAnswer: Haman offers to pay ten thousand talents of silver
questions.explanation: Esther 3:9-10 shows Haman proposing to pay ten thousand talents of silver before the king gives him his ring in 3:10.

questions.question: How does Esther 3:8 reflect the economic and legal tensions within the Persian empire?
options: It highlights that the Jews' laws differ and they do not keep the king's laws, implying social and legal tension.
It praises the Jews for obeying all laws.
It suggests the Jews have superior legal status.
It states that all peoples keep the same laws.
questions.correctAnswer: It highlights that the Jews' laws differ and they do not keep the king's laws, implying social and legal tension.
questions.explanation: Esther 3:8 emphasizes the Jews' distinct laws and non-obedience to the king's laws, signaling legal and cultural friction.

questions.question: In Esther 3:15, what cultural practice is implied by the king and Haman sitting down to drink after issuing the decree?
questions.explanation: Esther 3:15 shows the king and Haman sitting down to drink, reflecting Persian royal customs of feasting to celebrate decrees or alliances.

questions.question: True or False: According to Esther 3:2, Mordecai refused to bow or reverence Haman even though the king had commanded all servants to do so.
questions.explanation: Esther 3:2 explicitly states Mordecai did not bow or show reverence to Haman despite the king's command.

questions.question: True or False: Esther 3:14 indicates that the decree was kept secret and was not published to the people.
questions.explanation: Esther 3:14 states the writing was published to all people so they would be ready, indicating the decree was openly announced.

theological.title: Esther Chapter 3 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Esther Chapter 3 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Esther 3:2 teach about human sin in relation to civil authority?
options: Sin can manifest as rebellion against lawful authority
Sin is irrelevant to social hierarchies
Sinning against God always leads to immediate punishment
questions.correctAnswer: Sin can manifest as rebellion against lawful authority
questions.explanation: Esther 3:2 shows that Mordecai's refusal to bow to Haman, as commanded by the king, demonstrates sin as rebellion against civil authority.

questions.question: What doctrine about divine providence and human agency does Esther 3:10 teach?
options: God sovereignly uses human actions to accomplish His purposes
God relinquishes control when humans act wickedly
Human authority is independent of divine will
God directly causes evil through human agents
questions.correctAnswer: God sovereignly uses human actions to accomplish His purposes
questions.explanation: In Esther 3:10, the king gives Haman his ring, symbolizing delegated authority; this indicates divine providence working through human decisions.

questions.question: What doctrine about the nature of corporate identity and solidarity among God's people is taught in Esther 3:6?
options: The people of God share in both blessing and suffering corporately
Individual believers are solely responsible for their own fate
Corporate identity is irrelevant to divine judgment
Only the righteous individuals are affected by communal decisions
questions.correctAnswer: The people of God share in both blessing and suffering corporately
questions.explanation: Esther 3:6 reveals that Haman targets all Jews because of Mordecai, showing the corporate solidarity of God's people.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Esther 3:11 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Esther 3:11, where the king grants Haman authority to act against the Jews, shows God's sovereign rule over earthly powers.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is particularly highlighted in Esther 3:5 when Haman is full of wrath?
options: God's justice contrasted with human wrath
questions.correctAnswer: God's justice contrasted with human wrath
questions.explanation: Esther 3:5 shows human wrath exemplified by Haman, which contrasts with God's righteous justice.

questions.question: How does Esther 3:13 connect to the broader biblical theme of deliverance in Scripture?
options: It foreshadows the deliverance of God's people from impending destruction
It marks the final judgment with no hope for redemption
It shows God's abandonment of His covenant people
It emphasizes human effort over divine intervention
questions.correctAnswer: It foreshadows the deliverance of God's people from impending destruction
questions.explanation: The decree to destroy the Jews in Esther 3:13 sets the stage for God's deliverance, a recurring biblical theme (cf. Exodus 14).

questions.question: What redemptive-historical theme does Esther 3:7 prepare for in Scripture?
options: The sovereignty of God over time and chance
The establishment of the Mosaic Law
The exile of Israel to Babylon
questions.correctAnswer: The sovereignty of God over time and chance
questions.explanation: The casting of Pur (lots) in Esther 3:7 reflects God's providential control over 'chance,' a theme in biblical history.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Esther 3:4 and 3:5 teach about human sin and divine judgment?
options: Sinful rebellion provokes divine judgment through human agents
Sin has no consequences in this world
God directly punishes sin without human involvement
Sin is always hidden from human authorities
questions.correctAnswer: Sinful rebellion provokes divine judgment through human agents
questions.explanation: Verses 3:4–5 show Mordecai's disobedience leading Haman to wrath and seeking judgment against the Jews.

questions.question: What doctrine about the nature of evil and its ultimate purpose is taught by Esther 3:8 and 3:9 together?
options: Evil schemes against God's people ultimately serve His sovereign plan
Evil operates without any divine limitation
God approves of human evil for personal gain
Human evil always triumphs over God's people
questions.correctAnswer: Evil schemes against God's people ultimately serve His sovereign plan
questions.explanation: Haman's plot in Esther 3:8–9 is evil but it unfolds under God’s sovereign plan for ultimate redemption.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Esther 3:12 and 3:14 teach about the power of the written word in God's providence?
options: Written decrees have enduring authority and facilitate God’s providential plans
Written words are powerless without immediate fulfillment
God's will is only known through oral tradition
The written word is always subject to human error and irrelevant
questions.correctAnswer: Written decrees have enduring authority and facilitate God’s providential plans
questions.explanation: Verses 3:12 and 3:14 describe the king's letters, showing how written commands effect providential outcomes.

questions.question: Sceptics claim Esther 3:12-13 presents a divine endorsement of genocide. What does the passage actually teach?
options: It shows human abuse of delegated authority, not God's approval
It commands all believers to commit genocide
It promotes ethnic cleansing as a divine mandate
It is a historical myth with no theological relevance
questions.correctAnswer: It shows human abuse of delegated authority, not God's approval
questions.explanation: Esther 3:12-13 records the king’s decree issued by Haman’s influence, illustrating human sin and misuse of authority, not divine endorsement.

questions.question: What doctrine about human pride and its consequences is taught in Esther 3:1?
options: Pride leads to elevation but also to downfall
Pride is a virtue rewarded by God
Elevation in rank guarantees divine favor
Human status is unrelated to spiritual condition
questions.correctAnswer: Pride leads to elevation but also to downfall
questions.explanation: Haman’s promotion in Esther 3:1 highlights his prideful rise, setting the stage for his eventual judgment.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is most evident in Esther 3:15 when the city of Shushan is perplexed but the king and Haman drink?
questions.explanation: Esther 3:15 shows a contrast between human ignorance and God’s hidden providence, demonstrating His inscrutable wisdom.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Esther 3:3 and 3:4 teach about the social consequences of religious conviction?
options: Religious conviction can provoke conflict and persecution in a secular setting
Social norms always override religious duties
Religious convictions are private and have no public impact
questions.correctAnswer: Religious conviction can provoke conflict and persecution in a secular setting
questions.explanation: Mordecai's refusal to bow in Esther 3:3-4 leads to tension and persecution, showing the social cost of religious fidelity.

questions.question: What doctrine about material offerings as a means to influence authority is evident in Esther 3:9?
options: Material wealth is used to corrupt political decisions
Wealth has no role in spiritual or political matters
God endorses bribery for righteous causes
questions.correctAnswer: Material wealth is used to corrupt political decisions
questions.explanation: Haman’s offer of silver in Esther 3:9 shows the corrupting influence of wealth on political authority.
